rules.name: Honors (optional)
rules.desc:
The Honors Degree in Classics is designed for students who demonstrate exceptional academic performance and a commitment to scholarly research within the field. To qualify for this prestigious designation, students must fulfill the following criteria:
GPA Requirement: A minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.6 within the major is required to ensure a strong foundation in Classics.
Course Requirement: Upon approval of the final proposal, students may enroll in CLASSICS199
Undergraduate Thesis: Senior Research during their senior year. Participants can earn up to 6 units per term, with a total maximum of 10 units, which may contribute toward fulfilling major requirements. Candidates must complete an honors thesis, which serves as a capstone of their scholarly work.
Supervisor Selection: Students are required to select a tenure-track Classics professor or the Director of Undergraduate Studies to supervise their thesis.
Additional information, including the proposal submission deadlines, can be found on the Classics webpage.

rules.name: Core Requirement
rules.desc: Complete at least three of the following courses for a total of 15 units. Two of the three courses must be Classics 83 (The Greeks) and Classics 84 (The Romans).

rules.name: Depth Requirement
rules.desc:
Complete anywhere from 20-24 units of ancient history and civilization courses.
Suggested courses can be found below. Additional courses, including Latin, Ancient Greek, and Sanskrit (SNSKTLNG1-3) language courses, and IntroSems courses may count toward this requirement if approved by the Director of Undergraduate Studies.

rules.name: Breadth Requirements
rules.desc:
Complete at least 4 units in the areas “Greek and Roman Archaeology and art” and “Historical and social theory”, and at least 8 units in the area “Comparative ancient civilizations” as described below, so as to reach a total of 16-20 units.
Other courses may count toward this requirement with approval from the Director of Undergraduate Studies.
